chunks: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Saʿd, from Aḥmad, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Razīn, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a woman who had died: is it permissible for her husband to look at her face and her head? He said: “Yes.”

key_terms.أَيَصْلُحُ: is it permissible; asking about legal validity
key_terms.تُوُفِّيَتْ: she passed away; referring to the woman after death
key_terms.رَأْسِهَا: her head; another body part mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.لِزَوْجِهَا: for her husband; specifying the marital relationship
key_terms.وَجْهِهَا: her face; one of the body parts mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.يَنْظُرَ: to look; the act being ruled upon

ai.seo_question: Is a husband allowed to look at his deceased wife's face and head in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal ruling from Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام concerning a deceased wife. It indicates that it is permissible for her husband to look at her face and head after her death, and it is relevant to rulings connected to death and family law.
